chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who intentionally killed another man, then fled, and could not be apprehended until he died.
He عليه السلام said: “If he had wealth, it is taken from it; otherwise, it is taken from the closest relatives, then the next closest.”

key_terms.الْأَقْرَبِ فَالْأَقْرَبِ: the nearest relatives in order of kinship proximity
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth left by the offender

ai.seo_question: If an intentional killer dies before capture, from where is the financial compensation taken?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an intentional killer who dies before being apprehended. It states that financial liability is taken from his estate, and if he has no wealth, it is taken from his nearest relatives in order of closeness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5379 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Zharif ibn Nasih, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, who narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as)
regarding a man who intentionally killed another man and then fled, and he could not be captured until he died.
Imam (as) said: "If he had wealth, the blood money is taken from it. If he had no wealth, it is taken from his closest relatives, and then from those next closest to him."
